changelog:
v4.14.0 — The Newsletter Builder gets the new look

  • Nothing changes until a site turns the new look on. All of this only appears on a site that has ticked "Use the new PTA Hub look" in Newsletter settings — everywhere else the Builder works exactly as it did.
  • Saving a draft now says "Saved. Nobody sees it yet." with a NOT SENT YET stamp; publishing says "You're all set. Families can read it here." with a SENT stamp and the link; updating says "Updated. Families see the new version now."
  • After you publish, a "what's next" row offers Share it, Copy the email for GiveBacks, Start next week's, and I'm done — each one goes straight to something real.
  • The example newsletter now carries a clear EXAMPLE stamp where the publish button would be, so it's never mistaken for a real draft.
  • The Builder's own look — fields, buttons, help text, step navigation — now matches the rest of the new Hub look.
  • On a phone (782px and narrower), the live preview moves below the form behind a "Preview" button instead of crowding the screen, the five steps stay on one line you can scroll sideways, and every button is big enough to tap comfortably.

v4.13.0 — The simple view

  • Nothing changes when you update. All of this only appears on a site that has ticked "Use the new PTA Hub look" in Newsletter settings.
  • On a site that has: signing in lands on the PTA Hub, and the WordPress menu shows only the Hub and your profile — no Plugins, Appearance, Tools or other plugins’ menus to wade through.
  • Show all of WordPress is always one click away, in the toolbar and at the foot of the Hub home. Your choice is remembered, and it only affects you.
  • Nobody loses access: nothing about permissions changes, and every address still works if you type or bookmark it.
  • Hub screens are quieter — other plugins’ notices, Screen Options and the help tab stay out of the way.
  • New setting: who gets the simple view by default (everyone except administrators, to start). People can always switch for themselves.

v4.12.1 — Tidier wording on the new Hub screens

  • No line ends with a single word on its own any more, on any screen in the new look.
  • The two small links at the foot of the home screen no longer run together.

v4.12.0 — A new PTA Hub look, off until you turn it on

  • Nothing changes when you update. Every screen looks and works exactly as it did. The new look only appears on a site after someone ticks Use the new PTA Hub look on this site at the bottom of Newsletter settings, and it can be unticked again at any time.
  • With it on, Start Here becomes six plain questions — Tell families what’s happening, Answer a question families keep asking, Recommend someone we’ve used, Explain a PTA word, Fix something that’s wrong, and I’m not sure where to start — each leading to the screen that does it, with a single “Waiting for you” note when something needs a look.
  • It changes only what volunteers see when they sign in, never what families see on the website.

v4.11.0 — Newsletters can appear with your news posts (off by default)

  • New, both off until you turn them on, under Newsletter settings: Show newsletters with your news posts — a published newsletter also shows up in your news list, blog page, RSS feed, and its own "Newsletter" category, exactly like a regular post, without ever copying it — it stays one page. Covers your site's own blog list and a Beaver Builder or Ultimate Addons "Posts" module set to show posts.
  • Also add a short news post that links to it — an independent option that creates (and keeps up to date) a short, separate post with a summary, an "Inside this issue" list, and a button back to the full newsletter, every time you publish or update one. Turning it off leaves any posts it already made in place; unpublishing or trashing the newsletter drafts its linked post rather than deleting it.
  • Nothing changes on your website until you turn one of these on — updating to 4.11.0 does not.

v4.10.1 — Pick up your last newsletter from Start Here

  • The "Write this week’s newsletter" card now has an Edit No. 041-style button next to Start the newsletter, so you can go straight back to your latest issue.
  • The card now says five steps, matching the Builder.

v4.10.0 — Copy the newsletter email for GiveBacks

  • New on step 5 (Publish & share), once a newsletter is published: an Email (GiveBacks) section next to Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. It writes a ready-to-paste teaser email — the announcement, a short linked list of everything else in the issue, and one button back to the full newsletter, matching the newsletter email format — plus a Subject line suggestion. Copy subject and Copy email code put each on your clipboard, Preview the email shows it right there on the page, and a step-by-step "How to send it in GiveBacks," with screenshots, walks you through pasting it into GiveBacks' Newsletter Design editor.
  • Before you publish, this section shows a one-line note instead — "Publish first — the email links to your newsletter" — since every link in the email points at the newsletter's real web address.

v4.9.0 — Gentle length hints, and drag-and-drop that works on a phone

  • Fields with a length that reads best — like the announcement headline, an event title, or a footer link's wording — now show a quiet note once you're getting close, like "4 characters left," and a friendly "13 over — it may wrap onto another line" if you go past it. It never stops you from typing, saving or publishing — it's just a heads-up.
  • Fixed: Finish editing's drag-to-reorder didn't work on a phone or tablet at all. Dragging a section now works with a finger, a mouse, or a stylus. Press a row's handle and use the arrow keys to reorder without a mouse — it tells you where the section landed, like "Stories moved to position 3 of 6."

v4.8.2 — Coming up is calendar-only, plus Undo

  • Step 2's Coming up no longer mixes two different tools — it's calendar-only now. "Bring in your recent posts" moved to step 3 (Stories), where an imported post can still be added as a Date; the choice now reads "Date (goes to Coming up)" and, after adding, a short message says how many went there with a link straight to Coming up.
  • New: Undo. "Add selected"/"Add all" in the calendar and posts panels now show "Added N. Undo" right where you clicked, until you add again or close the panel — Undo removes exactly what that click added.
  • New: Remove all dates next to "+ Add event" once Coming up has two or more dates. Confirms in place (never a browser popup), then shows "Removed N dates. Undo" that puts them all back, in order.
  • The calendar panel's "Already added" rows now have their own small Remove link to pull just that one date back out of Coming up.
  • Fixed: after removing dates, the calendar panel could keep showing them as "Already added" until you closed and reopened it.
  • Fixed: adding or removing dates this way now properly triggers the "leave without saving?" warning, like every other change in the Builder.

v4.8.1 — Tidier recent-posts list

  • Post titles with apostrophes and quotes now show properly instead of codes like ’.
  • The Story / Event / Quick note choice only appears once you tick a post, so the list is much shorter to scan.
  • "Split into separate items" is only offered for posts that really have several sections.

v4.8.0 — Bring in your recent posts, plus fixes from live testing

  • New: Bring in your recent posts on step 2 (near Coming up) and step 3 (near Stories). If your school already posts announcements on the website, pull them straight into the newsletter instead of retyping. Pick a range (Last 2 weeks · Last month) or search, tick the posts you want, and choose Story, Event, or Quick note for each — we guess a sensible one for you. A post with a featured image and no words yet is flagged "Add a sentence or two"; a longer post is shortened to a couple of short paragraphs with a note that says so. A weekly roundup post (several sections in one post) offers "Split into separate items" so each part becomes its own story, event, or note. Posts already brought in show "Already added," even after you save and come back. Nothing on your website is ever changed — only your newsletter draft is filled in, and everything stays editable.
  • "Add from your calendar" now has a Select all / Clear and a one-click Add all, so a longer date range doesn't mean ticking every box by hand. New range: Next 3 months. "Bring in your recent posts" has the same Select all.
  • "Add from your calendar" and "Bring in your recent posts" were easy to miss, tucked far down the page. Step 2 now has a short line right at the top linking to both, and on Coming up the calendar/posts buttons are the main button until you've added something, then settle back to match "+ Add event."
  • Fixed: typed text in a Sign-off or story box could be cut off behind a scrollbar after just two lines. Every text box in the Builder now grows to fit what you type.

v4.7.1 — Calendar list skips past dates

  • "This month" in Add from your calendar now starts at the newsletter’s week, so events that already happened earlier in the month aren’t listed.

v4.7.0 — Add events straight from your Google Calendar

  • New setting: Google Calendar (for adding events) on Newsletter settings, separate from the calendar page link. Paste the calendar's public address, its plain calendar id, or a "share this calendar" link from Google Calendar — any of them work, and saving shows a plain result like "Found 42 upcoming events" or tells you exactly what to fix if the calendar isn't public yet.
  • Step 2 (What's happening) now has an Add from your calendar button above Coming up, once a calendar is set. Pick a range — This week, Next week, Next 2 weeks, or This month — tick the events you want, and click Add selected: each becomes an editable row with its date, title, and time/location filled in for you. Nothing is ever added automatically — you choose every event.
  • Events already in your newsletter show as "Already added" so you never get duplicates. Multi-day events (like school breaks) show as one row with "through …"; all-day events read "All day".

v4.6.1 — Share picture always shows the latest version

  • Fixed: after the share picture was redrawn, your browser could keep showing the old one. Each redraw now gets its own file, so you always see and save the current picture.

v4.6.0 — Share picture on every channel, and a better link preview

  • "Instagram square" is now called Share picture everywhere, because it is no longer just for Instagram. It, and everything that changes how it looks (photo, colors, framer, Upload your own), now live in ONE place at the top of Publish & share, with an "Adjust the picture" section you open only if you want to change something — so the page starts short.
  • Facebook and WhatsApp now offer the picture too: Facebook (which shows first) gets a note that picture posts get noticed more in groups, plus its own Save the picture button. WhatsApp gets a note that pasting the text alone already shows a preview of the newsletter, with the picture as an optional extra.
  • The phone page (from the QR code) now has a Facebook section to match, using the same wording.
  • A published newsletter now hands Facebook, WhatsApp and other apps a proper picture and one-line description for the preview card they show when the link is pasted, instead of your site's logo and a run-on sentence: the top story's own photo (or the share picture) as the image, and your one-line summary (or the announcement, or "Newsletter № 041 · Week of September 14") as the description. Works automatically with Rank Math; sites with no SEO plugin get this built in.

v4.5.3 — A photo framer that shows the whole photo, and an instant Instagram-square preview

  • The photo framer now shows the WHOLE photo, at its own shape, instead of a cropped preview — so the top of someone's head (or anything else near the edge) is never hidden while you're framing it. A bright box right on the photo shows exactly what will be kept; drag the dot, pinch or scroll to zoom, and the box follows.
  • Dragging the dot or zooming a photo behind the Instagram square's words now updates the picture instantly, right there in the Builder — no more waiting several seconds to see the result. The real picture still saves in the background; "Save the picture" waits for it to finish before handing you a file.

v4.5.2 — Instagram square with a photo, redone

  • A square with a photo now shows the photo clear and bright across the top, with the words on a solid band underneath — the photo is no longer hidden behind a dark bar.
  • The photo framer for the square is now wide, the same shape as the photo strip, so what you frame is what you get.
  • Phone photos that were saved sideways now come out the right way up.
  • "Bar color" is now "Band color".

v4.5.1 — Five more fixes from live testing

  • The Instagram square's photo bar no longer covers the whole picture — only a band behind the words now, so the photo stays visible above it.
  • The photo-privacy checkbox no longer stays ticked after a different photo is added — it resets (and asks again) whenever the newsletter's photos change, both on the main Publish & share step and the Instagram square's own photo.
  • The example newsletter can no longer be published by using Quick Edit, Bulk Edit, the block editor, or the API — it stays a draft no matter how you try to save it.
  • Jumping to a field that needs fixing now scrolls it to the middle of the screen, so the field and its message are both visible instead of one being cut off.
  • Every "Add image" button now reads "Change image" once a picture is chosen, and back to "Add image" after Remove.

v4.5.0 — Fixes from live testing

  • "Start from last issue" no longer copies the Top story's label — that was last issue's own headline, not a standing name. A new issue always starts with "Top story."
  • Each photo now shows a small preview with the focal dot right on it, and two buttons underneath — Whole photo and Crop to fit — instead of a hidden dropdown.
  • Fixed: dragging or zooming a photo now updates the live preview and the Instagram square right away, instead of only saving correctly behind the scenes.
  • When the Instagram square uses a photo, its words now sit on a solid color bar you choose (Text color and Bar color, next to "Use a photo behind the words") instead of a fixed dark scrim that could leave text unreadable. A plain warning shows if your two colors are hard to read together.
  • The last step is now two shorter steps: Finish editing (drag to reorder, with an Edit button on each section) and Publish & share (the photo check, Save/Publish/Update, and sharing). The Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp posts are now collapsible, one open at a time, so they don't all show in full at once.
  • After Save draft, Publish or Update, you now land on Publish & share, not back at the top of the order list.
  • Fixed: the first press of Publish could silently do nothing if a field elsewhere in the newsletter needed attention. Problems now show in plain language right where they are, with a summary and jump links, and Publish works on the first press.
  • A new "EXAMPLE — a finished newsletter (do not publish)" draft is created once for your site, so you can see what a finished issue looks like. It can never be published by accident.

v4.4.0 — Photos: crop, frame and zoom

  • Every newsletter photo — the top story’s and each story’s — can now stay Show whole (exactly like before) or switch to Crop to fit, a wide frame you point at what matters.
  • Framing a cropped photo has no slider: drag the dot on the photo itself, pinch or scroll to zoom, or use the keyboard (arrow keys move it, plus and minus zoom, hold Shift for bigger steps).
  • The photo picker now shows a real thumbnail of your picture instead of "Image #12 selected."
  • The Instagram square can now show a real photo behind its words instead of only a flat color — use your top story’s photo in one click, or choose a different one, framed the same drag-and-zoom way.
  • The photo-privacy checkbox now also covers the square’s photo, so the first time you add one there, it may ask you to confirm — same checkbox, same wording, only asked once.

v4.3.0 — Set it once

  • New Newsletter settings page (renamed from Sharing settings, same place under Newsletters) — set your Facebook group, Join the PTA link, Send us your news link, Calendar page link, and a contact email, once, and every newsletter after that carries them automatically.
  • The masthead now shows your school's actual logo (if you've set one under Appearance > Customize) with the site icon as a fallback, plus a "Join the PTA for {school year} →" link when you've set a Join link.
  • "What's coming up" now shows a "See full calendar →" link next to the heading, once you've set a calendar link and there's at least one date listed.
  • New: an automatic "Got news? Put it in the newsletter." closing appears right before the footer whenever you've set a news link, with your contact email if you've set one.
  • A brand-new newsletter now starts from your last issue: the footer, the top-story label and the quick-notes label are filled in for you, and the issue number is one more than last time. Stories, events, the announcement, the greeting and the summary all start blank, exactly like before.
  • The Instagram square now uses two colors you choose — a background and a text color — instead of one color on a fixed navy square. Pick both on the Newsletter settings page; leave either alone and it uses navy background / white text.
  • If you'd already set a share color, it still applies — it's now the square's text color instead of just an accent, so a couple of squares will look a little different once you open them again. Nothing about your saved color was lost.
  • Newsletters, Add New and Newsletter settings now live together under the main PTA Hub menu instead of their own top-level "Newsletters" entry. Old bookmarks and links still work.
  • "Start Here" now leads with a "Write this week's newsletter" card showing your last issue and a one-click Edit link.
  • As always: a setting you save today only affects newsletters you save or publish from today on — newsletters already sent don't change.

v4.2.0 — Newsletters look like the new site

  • The newsletter the builder publishes now matches issue № 040 and the redesigned site: one navy announcement at the top, stories on white with a "§ label" line, and the school's fonts.
  • The announcement has its own headline, a "When" line (your old short label moves here), an optional button, and dates you can add — past dates grey out on their own and the last one is shown as the deadline.
  • The button link can be a web address or just an email address, like leslie@example.org — it becomes an email link for you.
  • New: Quick notes, a short list of reminders and links under one heading.
  • The top of the newsletter reads "Newsletter № 041 · 2026–2027", with room for a one-line summary under the date.
  • Coming up shows the weekday under each date, and past dates fade.
  • The page no longer shows a second title above the newsletter.
  • Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp posts use the announcement's headline and mention your quick notes.
  • Newsletters you published before keep their old look until you open them and press Update.

v4.1.1 — Newsletter fixes

  • A published newsletter now stays published. Before, pressing Save draft or Preview on a live newsletter took it down and broke its link. A live newsletter now has Update and View newsletter buttons instead.
  • Creating or stopping a preview link no longer reloads the page, so nothing you've typed is lost. The builder also warns you before you leave with unsaved changes.
  • A published newsletter shows its real link, with Copy link, instead of offering a preview link that wouldn't work.
  • After you publish, the message has View newsletter and Copy link buttons and points you to the sharing tools below.
  • The photo check is remembered: reopen a published newsletter and the box is ticked, with the date. If a newsletter has no photos, you aren't asked at all. And if you forget the box, you're taken straight to it.
  • Sharing settings: type your color code (like 1a2f5c) instead of hunting for it in the color picker. Picking or typing a color selects "Use our own color" for you.
  • A site's first newsletter asks for the issue number instead of guessing No. 1. Issue numbers now read the same everywhere: № 042.
  • Event dates like "Sep 24" stay on one line.
  • The automatic headline names the week's Monday: an issue dated Wednesday, September 16 is "Week of September 14". A newsletter dated on a Sunday is named for the week ahead.
  • Removed a note saying the footer would be remembered for next time. It isn't yet.

v4.1.0 — Newsletters, and sharing them

  • New newsletter builder under Newsletters → Add New — four short steps (the basics, what's happening, stories, finish & publish) with a live preview beside the form, so you watch the newsletter take shape as you type.
  • Your school name, issue number and date are filled in for you, and the headline (“Week of September 14”) comes straight from the date.
  • Put the sections in any order, and send a preview link to someone before you publish.
  • New: Share this newsletter. The moment you publish, the last step hands you ready-to-paste posts for Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, written from what you already put in the newsletter. Nothing is posted for you — change anything you like, and your changes are kept.
  • Instagram gets a square picture made for you, in your school's color — or upload your own.
  • Posting from your phone? Scan the code on the last step to open the picture and the words there, ready to save and copy.
  • New Sharing settings under Newsletters: choose your school's color and add your PTA's Facebook group link.

v4.0.1 — Housekeeping & polish

  • Shared articles now keep their "who can see it" restriction when they appear on school sites — a Council article limited to certain roles stays limited everywhere.
  • Tidier styling — removed stray colored side-stripes so cards and notices look clean and finished.
  • The analytics chart no longer breaks when the charting library updates behind the scenes.
  • Old search and click logs are trimmed automatically (anything over 12 months), so the database stays lean.
  • Cleaner uninstall — removing the plugin now tidies up everything it created, across every school site.

v4.0.0 — One shared library, targeted and locked

  • Council articles can now be shared to all schools, only chosen schools, or kept Council-only — pick the audience right from the article editor.
  • Shared articles are read-only on school sites: a school can open and read a Council article but can't edit or delete it, so the Council stays the single source of truth.
  • Each school's own articles now rank first in that school's search, while a clearly stronger Council match still shows near the top.
  • Entry lists show a colored dot for each school (and a lock badge for Council articles) so you can tell at a glance who owns each entry — with new Ours / From Council / All filters. The Council can set each school's color under PTA Hub → School Colors.

v3.1.1 — Glossary & Hub links fixed on school sites

  • Fixed: on school (subsite) pages, the Knowledge Base and Glossary pages did not exist, so "Open the Hub" / "Open glossary" (and direct /knowledge-base and /glossary links) showed "page doesn't exist." Every school site now gets those pages automatically on the next admin visit after updating.

v3.1.0 — Welcome "Start Here" screen

  • New "Start Here" home base opens the moment you click PTA Hub — a friendly, welcoming landing page instead of a long list, so you always know where to begin.
  • A "Waiting for you" strip shows what actually needs attention right now — vendor reviews to approve, topic suggestions from members, and entries due for a fresh review — each with a one-click link straight to it. On a quiet week it simply stays empty.
  • Clear action cards point you to the few things you'll want to do: add or update an entry, manage the Vendor Directory, see the live Hub, or browse the glossary.
  • A new "PTA Hub — Start Here" panel on your main WordPress dashboard nudges you with the most pressing item and a button to jump right in.
  • Everything is role-aware — you only see the cards and nudges that apply to you, so nothing feels overwhelming.

v3.0.2 — Tidier Vendor Directory page

  • Removed the duplicate 'Vendor Directory' heading at the top of the page (your theme's automatic page title) so only the styled directory header shows — no more unfinished look.

v3.0.1 — Vendor links fix

  • Fixed: clicking a vendor that had been approved through the Vendor Approvals queue reloaded the directory instead of opening the vendor's page. Existing affected vendors are repaired automatically on the next admin visit.

v3.0.0 — Vendor Directory

  • New Vendor Directory — one shared list of trusted vendors (caterers, entertainers, printers and more) that appears on every school site
  • Browse vendors by category or search by name to find what you need fast
  • Read reviews from every PTA in the council — price and quality star ratings plus a "would use again" thumbs-up, each attributed to the school that wrote it
  • Write your own review right from the vendor's page — update it any time and it replaces your old one
  • Know a great vendor who isn't listed? Suggest them (with your first review) straight from the directory
  • Everything — new vendors and every review — is checked and approved by the Council before it appears, so you can trust what you read
  • The directory is members-only: log in to see vendor details and reviews

v2.9.1 — Wizard layout fixes

  • Content Wizard: the plus icon on "Add Step / Add Link / Add Item / Add Timeline Item" buttons now lines up with the label
  • Content Wizard: the "Related entries" panel no longer overlaps the "4 quick steps" bar — it now sits neatly beside the form and moves with the page when a banner appears

v2.9.0 — Trust polish (fewer dead ends, clearer answers)

  • Fixed the "+ Create Entry" link on Search Analytics → Content Gaps — it now opens the Content Wizard with the search term pre-filled instead of a permission error
  • Search and autocomplete now fully respect the "Require Login" setting and per-role restrictions — restricted entries no longer leak into suggestions, and results are no longer shared between users with different access
  • Search errors now show a "Try again" button instead of leaving you stuck
  • Content Wizard: if a save fails, you get a friendly red notice explaining what went wrong and your work is restored from autosave — no more white screens or lost fields
  • Choosing "Publish now" in the Wizard asks you to confirm before the entry goes live
  • Restricted entries now show a clear explanation of why you can't view them, with a "Back to the PTA Hub" button
  • Council-shared entries: the blue banner now explains what "shared from Council" means when you hover it
  • Review-status dots on the entries list now explain themselves in plain words on hover
  • Assorted cleanups behind the scenes

v2.8.0 — Motion polish (more natural, less in the way)

  • Content Wizard: dropped the 300ms height-animation when picking a category — the page no longer reflows under your scroll position on mobile
  • Wizard scroll-to-step trimmed from 400ms to 200ms
  • Wizard repeater add/remove now respects your OS "reduce motion" setting
  • FAQ "Copy Answer" button on single-entry pages now shows a green "Copied!" with checkmark for 1.5 seconds — no more silent click
  • Submit button shows a small press-down when clicked, so you know it registered
  • Link Insert modal in the Wizard now fades in gently instead of snapping
  • Category cards and search filter buttons show a 1px press when tapped (mobile-friendly)
  • Autosave "Draft saved" indicator now pulses briefly instead of lingering for 2.5 seconds
  • Tightened explicit transition properties so future layout changes don't accidentally animate

v2.7.0 — Frontend design polish (ease of use for non-technical volunteers)

  • Unified blue palette across every page — admin, search, single entry, glossary, suggest form
  • Bumped small body text to 14px minimum so older eyes can read it
  • Content Wizard: help text is now visible below each label (no more disappearing placeholder hints); added a "4 quick steps, ~5 minutes" scope cue at the top; required-field legend; more confident submit button
  • Front-end: tighter hero subtitle; a friendly "Coming soon" panel on brand-new sites with zero entries (plus a one-click "Add your first entry" shortcut for editors)
  • Single-entry page: lighter Table of Contents that doesn't compete with the article; explicit related-cards breakpoints at tablet/desktop; print + copy-answer buttons float to the top-right on wider screens
  • Post editor sidebar: PTA Hub meta boxes now share a subtle accent so they read as one group; Entry Details promoted to the top, QR Code and Network Sharing collapsed to the bottom
  • Visibility meta box now always shows current state ("Visible to everyone" or "Restricted") with collapsible controls
  • Search Analytics: visual bars next to every count make hot vs cold queries obvious at a glance
  • "Needs Review" dashboard widget: red dot next to each entry's last-reviewed date so urgency reads instantly
  • Suggest a topic form: live character counters, 5-character minimum, accent strip on the footer CTA
  • Suggestions queue: "Convert to Draft" row action now bold blue so it's distinct from the standard Trash action
  • Starter Content Importer: "already imported" warning now reads as a prominent yellow strip
  • Standardized all transition timings to 150ms and rounded all tags to pill shape

v2.6.3 — UI polish

  • Fixed misaligned icon on the "Create Entry" / "Update Entry" button in the Content Wizard

v2.6.2 — UI polish

  • Fixed misaligned plus icon on "Add Step / Add Link / Add Item / Add Timeline Item" buttons in the Content Wizard

v2.6.1 — Suggest a topic, related-entry hints in the Wizard

  • New public form lets parents and members suggest topics they wish were in the hub — submissions queue up under PTA Knowledge → Suggestions, ready to convert into drafts
  • "Suggest a topic" CTA now appears at the bottom of every single entry
  • The Content Wizard now suggests related existing entries based on the category and title you've entered — with a one-click button to insert a markdown link into your description
  • Internal: search engine refactored to expose a reusable PTK_Search_Engine::search() method

v2.6.0 — Reading time, QR codes, review reminders, preview links

  • Single entries now show estimated reading time and an auto-generated Table of Contents (entries with 3+ headings)
  • New "QR Code" sidebar in the post editor — download a PNG to print on table tents
  • "Last Reviewed" column and dashboard widget for stale entries (12-month threshold)
  • Generate a 7-day public preview link for draft entries — share with reviewers without giving them an admin login

v2.5.0

  • Print footer uses the site name automatically
  • Wizard defaults to Draft instead of Published
  • "Edit in Wizard" button on success screen
  • Editors can now see Search Analytics and Content Gaps
  • Public feedback widget no longer shows raw vote counts
  • Hub URL configurable via ptk_hub_slug option / ptk_hub_url filter

v2.4.0

  • Council entries auto-share to every school site by default
  • One-click "Sync all entries now" button on the Network Sync page
